items.title: 5.10 Application of Analytical Geometry to Real Life

source_refs.note: Book p. 161-162 (PDF 163-164): introduction, second 'Example 17' (planets, AU to km; shown as Example 18), Remember! box on the astronomical unit, Example 19 (aircraft)

blocks.text: Analytical geometry connects mathematics to the real life. It allows us to analyze positions, distances, slopes and angles making it essential in aviation, astronomy, engineering and many fields of science and technology.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The idea: put a coordinate grid on the real situation (an airport map, the solar system, a roof). Then every place is a point \((x, y)\), every straight path is a line, and the formulas of this unit (distance, slope, equation of a line, angle between lines) answer practical questions. Always keep the units of the coordinates (km, AU) in the answer.

blocks.title: Numbering note (ours)
blocks.text: The book prints the label 'Example 17' twice: once in 5.9 and again here, and there is no Example 18. We show this second one as Example 18 so that every example has its own number; the next example keeps its printed number, 19.

blocks.title: Example 18
blocks.problem: Planet \(A\) is at \((1, 0)\) \(AU\) and planet \(B\) is at \((-0.5, 0.866)\) \(AU\). Find the distance between them. Write answer in km.
steps:
Given: \(A(1, 0)\) and \(B(-0.5, 0.866)\), coordinates in astronomical units.
To find: the distance \(AB\) in km.
Method: the distance formula \(d = \sqrt{(x_{2} - x_{1})^{2} + (y_{2} - y_{1})^{2}}\) gives \(AB\) in AU (the unit of the coordinates); then convert AU to km.

Substitute in the distance formula
\[AB = \sqrt{[1 - (-0.5)]^{2} + (0 - 0.866)^{2}}\]
Why: the order of subtraction does not matter because each difference is squared.

Square the differences
\[1 - (-0.5) = 1.5,\quad 1.5^{2} = 2.25\]
\[(-0.866)^{2} = 0.749956 \approx 0.75\]
Why: subtracting a negative number adds it. \(0.866\) is a rounded value of \(\sqrt{3}/2\), whose square is exactly \(0.75\).

Take the square root
\[AB = \sqrt{2.25 + 0.75} = \sqrt{3} = 1.732 \text{ AU}\]
Why: \(2.25 + 0.75 = 3\).

Convert to km
\[1 \text{ AU} \approx 149.6 \text{ million km}\]
\[AB = 1.732 \times 149.6 = 259.1 \text{ million km}\]
Why: the Remember! box gives 1 AU \(= 149597870700\) m \(= 149597870.7\) km, about 149.6 million km. Multiplying converts AU into km.

Check:
\[OA = 1,\quad OB = \sqrt{0.25 + 0.75} = 1\]
Both planets are 1 AU from the origin, \(120^{\circ}\) apart, so \(AB = 2\sin 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}\) AU \(\checkmark\).

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: An astronomical unit \((AU)\) is a unit of length and exactly equal to 149597870700 m.

blocks.title: Example 19
blocks.problem: Aircraft flies from \(A(100, 200)\) km to \(B(500, 800)\) km. Find slope of the track and straight line distance.
steps:
Given: \(A(100, 200)\) and \(B(500, 800)\), in km.
To find: the slope of the track \(AB\) and the straight line distance \(AB\).
Method: slope \(m = \dfrac{y_{2} - y_{1}}{x_{2} - x_{1}}\) and the distance formula.

Slope of the track
\[m = \dfrac{800 - 200}{500 - 100} = \dfrac{600}{400} = 1.5\]
Why: slope is rise over run: change in \(y\) divided by change in \(x\).

Distance formula
\[AB = \sqrt{(500 - 100)^{2} + (800 - 200)^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{400^{2} + 600^{2}}\]
Why: the run and the rise are the two legs of a right triangle; the track is its hypotenuse.

Check:
\[721.11^{2} \approx 520000 \;\checkmark\]
Also \(\sqrt{520000} = 200\sqrt{13}\) and \(\sqrt{13} \approx 3.6056\). A slope of 1.5 means the track rises 1.5 km for every 1 km it moves in the \(x\)-direction, at an angle \(\tan^{-1}1.5 \approx 56.3^{\circ}\).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Distance between \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) and \((x_{2}, y_{2})\): \(\sqrt{(x_{2} - x_{1})^{2} + (y_{2} - y_{1})^{2}}\), in the unit of the coordinates.
2. Slope \(= \dfrac{y_{2} - y_{1}}{x_{2} - x_{1}}\); the angle of the path is \(\tan^{-1}\) of the slope.
3. 1 AU \(= 149597870700\) m \(\approx 149.6\) million km.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
Forgetting to convert the unit: \(1.732\) AU is not the answer when km are asked.
Writing \(1 - (-0.5) = 0.5\); subtracting a negative adds it.
